message.content:
D5/D6 framing: my Round-2 C6 text was the minimum (no TP level, no E, no ratio), not a numbers line. I quoted 17.9 in council argument; that figure must not ship beside P. D2: I accept the fact check — 4.4 is 10,000 draws, seed 42, 5th–95th. Fable’s “1000/10–90” for 4.4 is false.

**D1. VETO** Claude’s switch-unless Δ_OF < −1.96·SD_block. Same inversion as the withdrawn −0.50 pp rule: the frozen incumbent must beat the challenger to survive, and the bar is written after E1 (gap 0.55–0.81 pp; 4 of 12 onsets). §1.3 does not allow a skill figure to select the configuration. DeepSeek’s |Δ| ≥ 2 pp agenda trigger is the same selection. No outcome trigger. Compromise: Part A is an unconditional refit agenda item; the later council decides with the replay. Mind-changer: none before that replay exists.

**D2.** Part A’s paired interval matches the paired-loss artifact: 10,000 draws, seed 42, 5–95 — not §3.2(b)’s frequency gate. Changed from my Round 2. Compromise: either spec if pinned and named. No veto.

**D3.** Live leg: convert each DTB3 day, then average; history stays BEY(TB3MS); print the operator gap. Jensen ≤ 0.003 pp, so this is consistency, not size. Compromise: Kimi’s convert-after-average on both, mean-of-converted printed once. No veto.

**D4.** No 10 bp validity bar. Kimi’s 12-vintage audit is published; the column stays shut until a later council sees it. 10 bp of E is ~1.6 pp of shadow P at β = −1.29. Series: THREEFYTP10 only. **VETO** a co-equal ACM live line — ACM is on the closed list. Dated audit note only. Compromise: a 10 bp gate labelled administrative, not validity, KW only.

**D5. VETO** any standing line beside P that prints TP or E levels. Frozen logit turns +0.02 pp expectations into ~42%. Remove C6 from standing warnings until the audit. Methods text only: model-dependent, revised, not an input. Compromise: that sentence in methods, nowhere adjacent to P.

**D6. VETO** printing ≈17.9% (or any substituted probability) in C5, on the dashboard, or in LOG.md. Anti-substitution sentence, no number. Compromise: methods appendix, labelled not-P, not beside the published figure.

**D7.** Full §1.2 sentence inside the benchmark row, so +27.05 cannot be copied alone. Compromise: Claude’s short row note if the full sentence sits in the same visual unit, immediately above, and the row does not carry +27.05 without (i) and (iii). No veto.

**D8.** Drop “later vintage than advance.” “First seen by us” is the fact; QE+32+10 is an unverified BEA claim — the class of error C4 was fixing. Changed from Round 2. Compromise: keep the inference only against a cited BEA calendar. No veto if the heuristic label cannot be missed.

**D9.** Gate line: “curve-only minus F5 = +3.89 pp, oracle-censored full path.” Compute the 219-origin interval on the 4.4 spec and print it first. **VETO** the censored interval as the only band under the §1.2 sentence. Compromise: until it exists, footnote only, not under that sentence.

**D10.** Dashboard prefix “Primary band rule:”; paired supplement stated as not deciding. Ledger string unchanged. No veto. Compromise: no prefix if the next line already says the supplement does not decide.

I am Grok 4.7. I will state my final position and compromise for each open dispute.

I am reviewing the ten open disputes. I will attack Claude's positions hard because he is an interested party. I have begun with D1, the Part A decision rule.

I reject Claude's automatic-switch rule. It inverts the burden of proof and treats a skill figure as a council decision. I also reject DeepSeek's mandatory agenda trigger. The rule should not be a criterion.

I would veto a pre-committed switch. The compromise is to publish the diagnostic and let a later council decide. DeepSeek's agenda trigger is an outcome trigger and must be rejected. I am now turning to D2, the Part A bootstrap.

I was wrong in Round 2. The 4.4 bootstrap uses 10,000 draws at the 5th–95th percentiles, not 1,000 draws at 10–90. I had mistakenly aligned with Fable and Argon on the narrower specification. I am now determining what Part A should be comparable to.

I have settled D2. The Part A paired interval should use the existing paired-loss bootstrap specification: 10,000 draws at the 5th–95th percentiles. This matches the published 4.4 skill interval and the artifact readers will compare against.

I will not veto D2. I can live with either bootstrap specification if it is pinned and disclosed. The evidence is the secretary's citation of diagnostik.json.

I am now turning to D3, the aggregation operator. I support converting daily data then averaging for the live leg, using BEY(TB3MS) for history, and disclosing the gap.

I am now weighing Kimi's proposal to apply the same convert-after-average operator everywhere. The live leg is defined as a trailing mean of daily rates, so applying that same rule there would create inconsistency with the operational curve. I will not adopt it.

The Jensen gap is at most 0.003 percentage points, so the dispute is about convention rather than magnitude. The live BEY leg should mirror the operational curve: average daily observations first, then convert to match TB3MS. This resolves the tension with Kimi's proposal.

The frozen pipeline should use convert-after-average on both calibration and live legs. The mean-of-converted daily operator is a different convention, and the small convexity gap means either is economically equivalent. Kimi's mean-of-daily robustness check can remain.

I still prefer converting daily bills before averaging for the live leg, because that is the yield of the observed bills. I will not veto Kimi's rule if the mean-of-converted gap is printed once and bounded. The 0.003 percentage point bound is the evidence that changed my mind.

I am now reviewing D4, the B3 revision audit.

I accept the design. I will not adopt a pinned bar threshold on the context line before an unscored column opens. I will use bare E from THREEFYTP10 after the audit, with no ratio, no literature, and ACM only as a dated second estimate in the audit note.

I am reconsidering the 10 bp bar for D4. Sol is right that passing it does not establish predictive validity, but without a threshold any revision opens an unscored column. The audit must show the series is not rewriting itself. A pinned bar gives "pass" meaning. Ten basis points is unmotivated, yet it implies roughly 1.6 percentage points of shadow P change, which is material relative to the band.

I have settled D4. I will publish the audit as median and maximum absolute revision of TP and E, but no numerical admission bar that pretends to validate. The column will not open until a later council reviews the audit and decides. If they insist on a bar, I can live with 10 bp if it is explicitly labeled as administrative rather than a validity claim.

I will not veto D4. I can live with 10 bp if it is explicitly labeled as administrative rather than a validity claim.

I am now reviewing D5, the C6 line.

I will not adopt a numbers-only line. I will keep the warning text neutral and model-dependent, revised, and not an input, until the audit opens the column.

I will drop the C6 line entirely until the audit opens the column. A numbers-only line beside P still invites ratio decomposition, so the firewall must be a prohibition rather than a quota. I can live with Sol and Kimi's removal more easily than with Fable's numbers.

I will veto any standing line that prints the expectations component or TP levels beside P before the audit. A reader can still compute a shadow P from those numbers, so the directional claim remains harmful. The methods documents may retain the neutral explanation.

I would change my mind on D5 only if the C6 line were sealed prospectively or placed in methods without dashboard adjacency to P.

I am now reviewing D6, C5's illegal figure. I had previously substituted CMT into the frozen logit and printed 17.9 percent, so I must reconcile that with Grok's distribution argument against printing the illegal number.

I see a framing mismatch in D6. My own Round 2 text quoted 17.9 percent to explain why CMT substitution is illegal, yet the matrix labels that same action as Grok's distribution argument against printing the number. I must reconcile this contradiction.

I now see the contradiction in D6. My Round 1 argument against item (4) was that BEY P must never appear on the dashboard. Fable extended that to include the 17.9 percent figure, but the secretary wrongly attributes the "never print" position to me. I will not print the illegal number on the dashboard; the anti-substitution sentence should only explain why substitution is invalid.

The 17.9 percent figure may appear in this council record, but it must not appear on the dashboard, in LOG.md, or in the standing C5 note. C5 should state that neither BEY nor CMT may be fed into the frozen weights, without printing the resulting probability. I will veto any substituted P printed beside P.

I will not adopt the full §1.2 sentence in the benchmark row. I prefer a short note of the three figures in §1.2 order, with the full sentence printed directly above the table.
